CD34+ marrow cells travelling between states

Cells hop from measured cell to measured cell, steered by the scJDO2 drift (direction from pseudotime), so they always stay on real cells. They start in HSC and change colour as they move into a new state.

Hover a gene or an edge.

How this was made. 5,780 cells, 2,002 variable genes, a 10-dimensional latent space. Direction comes from pseudotime: the local gradient of pseudotime. This is a gradient field by construction, the weakest source: it says which way is later, nothing about rotation or regulation, and the operator will be mostly symmetric. scJDO2's MeasuredDrift is fitted to it on 5,780 cells (median cosine 0.62); the gene-level operator and archetypes are fitted on 2,000 cells sampled across states.

Walkers hop between measured cells. Each cell links to its 30 nearest cells in the latent space, and a hop to neighbour j is weighted by exp(cos(xj − xi, drift at i) / 0.25), the CellRank-style velocity kernel; about 150 hops per walker. 300 walkers start in HSC. At the end: Mono 81, Ery 33, CLP 2, DCs 184. The floor is UMAP of the latent space; the surface (valleys from cell density, slope from the projected drift) is a backdrop only. Playback counts hops, not time.

Median cosine between the drift and the direction of increasing pseudotime 0.59.
